evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: albino Dunkin/Hartley guinea pigs. Test material: 25% active palmityl/stearylamidopropyl dimethylamine in 8.95% phosphoric acid and 66.05% water. evidence.support_text: Palmityl/stearylamidopropyl dimethylamine at 25% active in 8.95% phosphoric acid and 66.05% water was studied for delayed contact hypersensitivity using albino Dunkin/Hartley guinea pigs. evidence.support_text: Hill Top Research, Inc performed a delayed contact hypersensitivity study of stearamidopropyl dimethylamine in guinea pigs. One guinea pig had delayed contact hypersensitivity; no reactions in controls. Rechallenge at 0.25% gave one positive out of six. The study concluded the material caused delayed contact hypersensitivity.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Phase III of provocative use test: full use of shampoo, body wash, and hand soap containing CAPB-F (5.0-5.2% active) for 3 weeks; 10 participants
evidence.support_text: In phase III, 3 participants had scalp, face, and/or neck and body dermatitis.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Products containing CAPB-F grade (shampoo 5.0% active, hand soap and body wash 5.2% active); phases I (forearm wash with 10% shampoo) and II (daily shampoo use); 10 participants with prior positive patch test to 1% CAPB
evidence.support_text: Seven participants had erythema, scaling, and pruritus on the arms, face, and/or neck in either phase I or II of the study. Three participants completed the product use phases without experiencing an allergic reaction.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Rohm & Haas skincare preparation preserved with 15 ppm MCI/MI, twice daily for 7 days
evidence.support_text: A Rohm & Haas skincare preparation preserved with 15 ppm MCI/MI caused reactions in 40% of 20 MCI/MI-allergic subjects.

evidence.experimental_conditions: shampoo preserved with 0.3% imidazolinyl urea (IU), 6 applications over 14 days
evidence.support_text: In the same double-blind trial, 2 subjects experienced severe adverse reactions to the shampoo preserved with 0.3% imidazolinyl urea, leading to discontinuation after 1 or 2 washes.

evidence.experimental_conditions: shampoo preserved with 15 ppm MCI/MI, 6 applications over 14 days
evidence.support_text: In a double-blind crossover trial, 27 subjects patch-test-positive to 100 ppm MCI/MI used a shampoo preserved with 15 ppm MCI/MI. 3 of 27 subjects developed allergic reactions to the MCI/MI-preserved shampoo, with some discontinuing due to severe reactions.

evidence.experimental_conditions: shampoo preserved with 25 ppm MCI/MI, use under presumed normal conditions
evidence.support_text: In a study with experimentally sensitized volunteers, all 4 subjects exposed to a shampoo preserved with 25 ppm MCI/MI developed a reaction to the product.

evidence.support_text: A skin lotion preserved with 15 ppm MCI/MI elicited reactions in 57% of 7 MCI/MI-allergic subjects.

evidence.support_text: In a study with 18 experimentally induced MCI/MI-allergic volunteers, various rinse-off products preserved with MCI/MI (4–6 ppm) were used for 3–6 weeks. No skin reactions indicative of allergic contact dermatitis elicitation were observed.

evidence.experimental_conditions: lotion containing 0.1% Euxyl K400 applied to antecubital fossa twice daily, 11 Euxyl K400-allergic patients, reaction after 5 days
evidence.support_text: Tosti et al. performed a double-sided provocative use test in 11 Euxyl K400-allergic patients; 5 patients reacted with dermatitis after 5 days in the fossa challenged with lotion containing 0.1% Euxyl K400.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Normal daily hygiene use of shower gel containing CAPB; 4 weeks
evidence.support_text: Only 7 participants participated in phase III and no adverse reactions were observed.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Rinse-off cosmetic products containing 4-6 ppm MCI/MI, used for 3-6 weeks in 18 healthy volunteers
evidence.support_text: Weaver et al. performed a 3–6-week provocative use test with different rinse-off cosmetic products containing 4–6 ppm MCI/MI. No dermatitis reactions were found in 18 healthy volunteers (171).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Occlusive patches were induced thrice per week for 3 weeks, maintained for 24 h. Tested in shampoos containing 12.5 ppm CMIT/MIT. Subjects: 1450 individuals.
evidence.support_text: In a repeated patch test of CMIT/MIT in 1,450 individuals using occlusive patches thrice per week for 3 weeks, only one or two cases of skin sensitization occurred in shampoos containing 12.5 ppm of CMIT/MIT.

evidence.experimental_conditions: rinse-off products (liquid soap, shampoo, hair conditioner, liquid fabric softener, bath foam, shower foam) containing CMI/MI 4-6 ppm; daily use for 3-6 weeks; 18 volunteers
evidence.support_text: Weaver et al. tested rinse-off products containing CMI/MI at 4-6 ppm on 18 CMI/MI-sensitized subjects over 3-6 weeks and observed no allergic clinical contact dermatitis.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.3% diazolidinyl urea (730 ppm free formaldehyde); 30 formaldehyde-allergic patients; exposure first in antecubital fossa for 2 weeks, then on neck/face for negative cases
evidence.support_text: Zachariae et al. found that 7 patients reacted to 0.3% diazolidinyl urea (730 ppm free formaldehyde).

evidence.assay_type: repeated open application test (ROAT) with deodorant
evidence.experimental_conditions: 8 patients with prior hypersensitivity to cinnamaldehyde; deodorant containing 0.032% cinnamaldehyde applied twice daily for 2 weeks
evidence.support_text: In a ROAT with deodorant, 8 dermatitis patients with prior patch test reactions to cinnamaldehyde were exposed to a deodorant containing 0.032% cinnamaldehyde twice daily for two weeks; 2 patients reacted (low-dose).

evidence.experimental_conditions: irradiation with ultraviolet light
evidence.support_text: Sodium omadine has been shown to bind covalently to human serum albumin on irradiation with ultraviolet light.

evidence.experimental_conditions: βNF-induced rat liver microsomes; NADPH-regenerating system; concentration of 3,5-diCH3-PAR not specified; GSH (4 mM) added after formation.
evidence.support_text: Rat liver βNF-induced microsomal cytochrome P450-catalysed oxidation of 3,5-diCH₃-PAR formed a product with UV-absorbance similar to authentic 3,5-diCH₃-NAPQI. The absorption at 274 nm was abolished upon addition of GSH (4 mM).

evidence.experimental_conditions: HRP/H₂O₂ system; 3,5-diCH3-NAPQI formed; then BSA (1.5 mM) added.
evidence.support_text: When 3,5-diCH₃-NAPQI was formed in the HRP/H₂O₂ system, addition of an excess amount of bovine serum albumin (1.5 mM) changed the UV spectrum to one similar to that of 3,5-diCH₃-PAR, indicating protein binding.
